AquaLoop Value Proposition The Core Engine

Commercial towers discharge washbasins and ablution greywater daily while flushing urinals and irrigation using potable drinking water. AquaLoop closes this loop with a configurable physical treatment train paired with a Digital Twin Control Layer that balances throughput, pump affinity laws, and backwashing to live demand.

Prototype Pitch: "AquaLoop turns a building's wastewater stream into a managed water resource. It recovers washbasin and ablution greywater, treats it to non-potable reuse standard, and runs every pump, membrane and dose on dynamic setpoints so building owners save mains water, energy and money—with auditable proof."

Eight-stage treatment train and intelligent control layer for washbasin and ablution recovery:

Process Flow Highlights: Integrates coarse pre-screening, equalisation buffering (≤24h), primary feed pumps with disc filters, optional biological polishing (MBBR), ultrafiltration (UF), sodium hypochlorite disinfection, air-gapped treated storage, and VSD booster delivery.

Empirical Evidence Base Literature & Field Calibration

Figures quoted from verified peer-reviewed articles, regulatory filings, and green building standards.

Source & Reference Key Finding & Measured Data AquaLoop Implementation & Caveats
Oh et al. (2018)
J. Cleaner Production		 Greywater represents 43–70% of total domestic wastewater volume. Proposed Malaysian urban reuse targets: pH 6–9, TSS <20 mg/L, <5 NTU, BOD₅ <20 mg/L, <10 CFU/100 mL E. coli. Used to establish source segregation strategy and water-quality safety limits. Caveat: 43–70% is domestic wastewater; not guaranteed in every office tower.
Habibullah et al. (2023)
Planning Malaysia		 Malaysian green office building recorded 520.6 m³ of washbasin/ablution greywater in 60 days (8.7 m³/day). Non-potable reuse supplied 28.1% of water demand (752.6 of 2,676.9 m³). Core empirical calibration basis for AquaLoop's pilot design. Caveat: Single building observed over 2 months in 2020; treatment energy was not reported.
Leong et al. (2019)
J. Cleaner Production		 Tropical LCA/LCC study: Hybrid commercial rainwater-greywater achieved 55.3% mains-water saving. Systems financially unviable at 6% discount rate without green incentives. Underpins AquaLoop's lifecycle cost optimizer and GTFS 4.0 financing integration. Caveat: 55.3% applies to hybrid setups, not greywater alone.
Leong et al. (2018)
J. Cleaner Production		 In tropical conditions, greywater recycling met 21.1% of commercial flushing and irrigation demand. Commercial systems should reuse greywater first, topping up with rainwater. Directly informs AquaLoop's source priority logic: Greywater first → Rainwater second → Air-gapped mains last.
Soong et al. (2021)
RMTB Journal		 Survey of 91 Klang Valley construction players: Lack of awareness was the biggest barrier (4.10 / 5.0) and client-support readiness was lowest (3.31 / 5.0). AquaLoop solves this barrier by delivering clear, live levelised cost (RM/m³) and ESG compliance dashboards.
Sulaiman et al. (2026)
JTHEM		 No specific Malaysian statutory act governs greywater treatment. Benchmarked California Title 22 and European standard EN 16941-2:2021. AquaLoop adopts international performance benchmarks and logs all inline telemetry for local authority audits.
UTS-ISF for AWRC (2013)
Darling Quarter Study		 Building plant tuning, blower optimization, and analyzer-based chlorine dosing cut specific energy from 7.2 to 4.6 kWh/m³ (36% reduction) within 8 months. Validates that algorithmic pump control delivers real, measurable OPEX savings. Caveat: Measured on mixed-wastewater MBR with RO.
SFPUC (2025)
Onsite Reuse Program		 Mandatory onsite reuse for commercial developments ≥100,000 gross sq ft in San Francisco. Serves as global precedent for master-planned township integration.

Lifecycle Costing & Malaysian Tariff Calculator Verified 2025/2026 Inputs

Water savings alone rarely justify small decentralized systems without sizing and energy optimization.

Verified Malaysian Tariff Framework (Checked Oct 2026)

  • Selangor Commercial Water Tariff: RM 3.51/m³ for first 35 m³/month; RM 3.83/m³ for excess consumption (Air Selangor/SPAN, effective Sept 2025).
  • Commercial Electricity: Regulatory Period 4 (RP4) base tariff average of 45.4 sen/kWh (effective July 2025).
  • Peninsular Grid Carbon Intensity: 0.740 kg CO₂e/kWh (Provisional factor, Energy Commission Malaysia 2024/2026).

Financing & Green Incentives

  • Green Technology Financing Scheme (GTFS 4.0): Offers 60% government loan guarantee on green CAPEX and a 1.5% p.a. interest rebate (extended to 31 Dec 2026).
  • Green Investment Tax Allowance (GITA): 100% tax allowance on qualifying capital expenditure for approved green building technologies.
  • Payback Multipliers: Commercial payback accelerates dramatically when scaled beyond single offices to retail centers and township clusters.

Rule-Based Safety Interlock Simulator Zero-Trust Guard

Safety decisions are executed strictly by deterministic hardware logic—never generative AI.

Identified Hazard Operational Risk AquaLoop Engineering Mitigation
Water Quality & Odour Pathogens reach toilet fixtures; greywater turns septic if stagnant. Hold-time strictly capped at ≤24 hours; continuous inline Cl₂ dosing; auto sewer divert.
Cross-Connection Accidental contamination of municipal drinking water system. 100% separate, color-coded piping network; physical air gap on mains water top-up.
Membrane Bio-Fouling Soaps and surfactants cause irreversible flux loss and membrane burnout. Rotary pre-screening, variable disc filters, TMP-triggered backwashing, and automated CIP.
Regulatory Compliance Gap Absence of specific Malaysian federal greywater statutory acts. Design adheres to US EPA Water Reuse & European EN 16941-2:2021 standards.
